title: Per-client warmup manifest and rollout crib
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal crib for per-client warmup flows, soft pin strategies, and lightweight operational runes. This is a scratchpad — not final. The goal: reduce cold-latency surprises and unit-cost blips when flipping tenants to a new model variant or quantization level.

Context / motivation:
- We keep seeing transient latency spikes on first few requests after a model flip for mid-to-high token workloads. Root cause tends to be KV-cache misses + kernel warmup + dynamic batching lull.
- Enterprise customers with bursty usage (tick-based agents, scheduled reports) are sensitive to the first-10-requests tail. They want predictable first-response SLOs.
- We need a replicable, low-friction per-tenant warmup checklist that SRE/SEs can run or that the SDK can trigger as part of a pin flow.

High-level approach:
1) Identify warmup cohorts: sequenced buckets per client (pilot small anchor cohort -> gradual ramps).
2) Run warmup steps in order (head priming, synthetic cache fill, slow-ramp traffic).
3) Observe sentinel metrics and only advance when safe.
4) If any sentinel trips, pin back and run remediation steps.

Warmup checklist (operational steps):
- Preflight (manual or via automation):
  - Confirm model variant and quantization profile chosen. Embed the variant tag in the rollout ticket.
  - Reserve a small dedicated capacity window (if on Dedicated) or schedule low-traffic timeframe (Hosted: off-peak region).
  - Notify on-call and customer success (short Slack note + ticket link).
  - Sanity-run unit test prompts via dry-run endpoint to ensure model loads.

- Stage 0: head priming (0–2 minutes):
  - Send 3 tiny canonical prompts (short completions) from the tenant to warm RT kernels and KV structures.
  - Targets: <50ms extra tokens CPU/GPU init. If >2x typical, abort.

- Stage 1: KV prefix seeding (2–8 minutes):
  - For typical tenant patterns, replay recent legitimate prompts (capped at 20 requests) to build per-tenant cache entries.
  - If tenant uses session-based prompts, seed the session sequence including system and user instructions.
  - Note: avoid replaying private customer data in logs; mark these warmup requests as non-PII and set sampling off for traces.

- Stage 2: slow ramp (8–30 minutes):
  - Gradually increase to 5–10% of normal qps for tenant for 10 minute blocks. Monitor latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and error rate.
  - Look for sign of gradual KV hit-rate improvement and reduced per-token compute on repeated prefixes.

- Stage 3: traffic handover (30–60 minutes):
  - If all sentinels green, reassign traffic to 100% variant or release SDK toggle.
  - Keep elevated telemetry retention for +2h to watch for regressions.

Sentinel metrics (advance only if all green):
- p50 latency <= baseline * 1.2
- p95 latency <= baseline * 1.5 (if p95 spikes but p50 stable, throttle and observe)
- error rate increase < 0.1% absolute
- KV cache hit-rate trend: rising or within expected band
- Unit token cost drift < 8%
- Model hallucination QA sample passes (run 20 eval prompts, compare to baseline embeddings similarity > 0.9)

Rollback triggers (immediate pinback):
- Any increase in customer-facing error codes (5xx / 429) beyond +0.2%
- p99 > baseline * 2 for > 5 minutes
- Unexplained drop in KV hit-rate or repeated OOMs

Remediation playbook (quick):
- Soft pin to previous variant (automated via API)
- If GPU OOMs: scale up temporarily and re-run Stage 0–1 with smaller prefixes
- If latency: investigate kernel selection mismatch (check runtime logs), force recompile path or switch to stable kernel alias
- If model quality regression: immediate pin + open eval ticket, notify product & ML leads

Client categorization heuristics (for choosing warmup depth):
- Tiny (low qps, <10 req/hr): head priming + 2 synthetic sessions
- Small (10–200 req/hr): full Stage 0–2, 30m observation
- Medium (200–2k req/hr): full pipeline + 60m warmup and extended telemetry retention
- Large (>2k req/hr or SLA customer): reserve dedicated warmup capacity + stakeholder signoff

Operational notes and safety knobs:
- Keep TTL for cached prefixes limited (configurable per-tenant). If tenant is cold > 24h, schedule re-prime before major flips.
- Use SDK flag warmup=true to mark requests so Console doesn't count them against billing dashboards.
- Add a non-PII header X-RI-WARMUP to isolate in logs and traces.
- Provide an API endpoint /warmup/seed that customer SEs can call to run canonical sequences (auth required).

Telemetry & dashboards to add (notes for product/observability):
- Warmup cohort dashboard: per-tenant KV hit-rate, first-10-requests latency, warmup step timestamps
- Canary comparison: side-by-side p50/p95/p99 for old vs new variant over time windows
- Heatmap of token-cost delta during warmup; flag big outliers

Questions and unresolved items (TODOs):
- How to safely seed user-specific session contexts without storing sensitive content? (Consider ephemeral obfuscation)
- Should warmup requests be free for customers? We currently mark them but still bill; policy needs product confirmation.
- Need a minimal SDK helper (JS/Python) that implements the staged warmup flow and backoff for public examples. Create tracking ticket.
- Evaluate whether quantization changes need a different warmup (e.g., re-run small held-out eval set).

Quick operational cheatsheet (one-liners):
- "If p99 blows up within 10 minutes, pin back and scale up. Dont' iterate with more traffic."
- "Mark warmup traffic in traces (X-RI-WARMUP) and dont' surface on customer dashboards."
- "Use small canonical prompts first, then seed longer session prefixes."

References & links: (put full links in ticket)
- Confluence: warmup patterns doc (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: rollout ticket template (JIRA-RINF-987)
- PR: sdk-warmup-helper (github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/412)

Notes to self: keep this short and convert to a slide deck for SE onboarding. Add a minimal curl example for /warmup/seed. Run a dry-run with Maya next Tue.

End of scratch.
